summary:
Verdict: 10 CONFIRMED, 2 DOWNGRADE, 0 REFUTED, 0 UNVERIFIABLE. The gate decode survives adversarial re-reading — I re-ran every command against dumps/s129-poolgate rather than checking the quotes, and independently re-derived the two hardest links (the 49-entry UWorld property array and the 155-entry ALokiGameState array) with my own scripts rather than trusting the walk.

The load-bearing conclusion stands and is stronger than reported: ULokiActorPoolManager's vtable slot 90 (disp 0x2D0, arithmetic verified at the live call site 0x33560C5) returns ALokiGameState::bSupportsActorPoolPriming, read as byte [W->GameState + 0x898], and the base class contributes nothing (0x0B9E1F0 = the universal `mov al,1; ret` fold, 26444 qword pointers, correctly left unnamed). I confirmed the branch polarity at the consumer myself — 0x33560CB `test al,al; jne` means the FALL-THROUGH is the logging path, and strxref puts the single code reference to 'Feature is not enabled' at 0x33560DC inside PrimePools.

Three things I checked that the original did not, all of which strengthened it: (1) at the exact address the repo retraction cites, 0x5608FB8, the instruction is literally `mov rsi,[rsi+0x258]` with rsi = the GetWorld return — the sharpest possible form of claim [4]'s reconciliation; (2) a positive control for CPF_Net that claim [10] lacked — 43 of 155 ALokiGameState properties DO carry bit 0x20, including CurrentPhase@0xa44, so the mask discriminates on this very array; (3) the sole qword pointer to the Loki override 0x56363F0 is 0x8877D50 = its vtable + 0x2D0 exactly, and a third independent naming of 0x5380690 via FClassRegisterCompiledInInfo@0x89890C0 -> U'ALokiGameState'. All 17 addresses are on decrypted pages (fkdis cov = present), so no absence claim here is coverage-blocked.

The two downgrades are both grading/wording defects, not wrong conclusions. [1]: `vtables.py name AActor` returns nothing and AActor is absent from the tool's 5076-class index, so "AActor [49] = 0x338C990" was never measured — it is inferred from four AActor-derived classes (I added APawn as a fourth). [5]: "BYTE-FOR-BYTE twin" is literally false — the two sites differ in the rcx setup (3 bytes vs 7) and in the jump width; they are the same compiler idiom, which is all the corroboration needed, but "byte-for-byte" is a measurable property the sequences fail. Two smaller evidence nits worth fixing in place: [6] mis-attributes `mov rax,[rip+0x4ca178f]` to the jne target (it is at 0x5380732 on the fall-through; the target 0x5380739 is only `add rsp,0x78; ret`) and calls a qword-pointer count a "fold multiplicity"; [3] writes the property array as "0x825DFA0..0x825E120 = 49 entries", where the stated arithmetic yields 48 — the half-open end is 0x825E128, which FClassParams+0x18 independently corroborates.
